annotation.title_clean: Durkheim’s Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.title_en: Durkheim’s Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.venue: Social Robots in Social Institutions: Proceedings of Robophilosophy 2022 (Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 366), IOS Press
annotation.summary_en: Robophilosophy 2022 conference paper (abstract only) applying Durkheim's theory of the division of labor and social solidarity to workplace robotics. It argues that robots may contribute to the social pathologies Durkheim identified: forced division of labor, excessive division of labor and anomie. It proposes a form of socially responsible innovation that accounts for these effects.
key_provisions_or_claims: Durkheim's threefold social pathology (forced division of labor, excessive division of labor, anomie) offers a framework for assessing the social and ethical impacts of workplace robots
Organic solidarity rests on interdependence created through the division of labor
Robots can contribute to pathologies that disrupt organic solidarity
Socially responsible robotics innovation should account for Durkheim's insights
